papers.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
papers.abstract: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $\Gamma$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $\Gamma = 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

papers.title: Learning a model of non-stationary nuisances with non-local correlations for object detection
papers.abstract: We tackle the problem of detecting faint objects in multivariate data corrupted by a strong and spatially correlated nuisance component in the low-sample regime. Standard covariance-based models often yield unstable or ill-conditioned estimators of the nuisance statistics, severely degrading detection performance. We propose a data-driven approach based on sparse precision matrix modeling, where the precision matrix is approximated through a pivoted sparse Cholesky factorization whose non-zeros coefficients are learned by maximum likelihood. This yields a low-complexity yet expressive statistical model of the nuisance. Building on this model, we derive a generalized likelihood ratio test for faint source detection enabling direct control of the false alarm rate. The approach is evaluated on an astrophysical application: the detection of exoplanets by high contrast imaging, where it achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers.title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
papers.abstract: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. We reanalyze all of these bounds for the couplings to photons, electrons and nucleons. Space-based tests are weakened by several orders of magnitude, whereas the terrestrial tests are suppressed far more strongly and lose their sensitivity at low masses. As a result, for each coupling, $f$-dependent windows in the parameter space open up. For a coupling to nucleons a window persists at large couplings even for $f\sim 100 \,\rm{GeV}$. In particular, no current experiment constrains couplings between the naive limit and the stellar-cooling bound in a window of masses above $\text{few}\times 10^{-12}\,$eV, a range of more than ten orders of magnitude in coupling. This presents a unique opportunity for a ground-space clock comparison test to probe uncharted territory.

papers.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
papers.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

papers.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
papers.abstract: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $\Lambda$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $\Lambda\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_\delta$ and second-order $b_{\delta^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

papers.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

papers.title: Revisiting the centrifugal breakout scaling relationship for H$$ emission in light of $$ Oph C, the coolest B-type star with an H$$-bright centrifugal magnetosphere
papers.abstract: The corotating magnetospheres of B-type stars are strongly affected by magnetic field strength and rotational velocity, which determine both the geometry and strength of visible and radio emission; however, H$\alpha$ emission largely disappears below a bolometric luminosity of $\log{(L / L_\odot)} \sim 2.8$. The nearby B5 V star $\rho$ Oph C (HD 147932) is the least-luminous rapidly rotating magnetic B-type star to display magnetospheric H$\alpha$ emission. While $\rho$ Oph C's radio magnetosphere has been extensively studied, its magnetic field and H$\alpha$ magnetosphere have been constrained only via snapshot observations. We present a new dataset of high-resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetry covering the star's rotational period, which is revisited by combining Hipparcos, K2 and TESS photometry. We find that the star's magnetic field strength and geometry are consistent with the model inferred from radio data. As expected from the magnetic model, there is very little variability in H$\alpha$. Comparison of the light curve to both equivalent width measurements from metallic lines and magnetospheric models suggests that the star's photometric variability is dominated by surface chemical abundance spots; however, there is complex rotationally modulated variability at about the mmag level which probably originates in the magnetosphere. $\rho$ Oph C is the least luminous B-type star in which magnetospheric H$\alpha$ emission has yet been detected, and its emission is notably weaker than the predictions of the centrifugal breakout model. Its photometric eclipse depth is also much lower than predicted by the CBO model. However, its radio luminosity is consistent with CBO predictions. We speculate on this basis that $\rho$ Oph C may be a transitional object between effective temperature regimes with hydrogen-dominated and decoupled metallic winds.

papers.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
papers.abstract: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. These conditions serve as an analog of ice nucleation in cold astrophysical and atmospheric environments. The ice grains form without the presence of particulate impurities, and do not form in the absence of ionization, indicating that nucleation is induced by ions. Time-resolved ion mass spectrometry provides separate detection of clusters of water molecules on both positive and negative ions. Hydrated negative ions, mainly $\mathrm{OH^-(H_2O)_n}$, grow to $\sim$200 amu, while hydrated positive ions, mainly $\mathrm{H^+(H_2O)_n}$, remain small and short-lived. As the temperature is reduced from room temperature toward 200 K, negative ion clusters grow in size and then drop sharply in abundance, consistent with the onset of rapid growth into macroscopic ice grains below a critical temperature. This indicates that hydrated negative ions are key precursors to ice nucleation in cold, weakly ionized environments, such as the Earth's mesosphere and protoplanetary disks, providing a concrete pathway for ice formation in environments where the nucleation mechanism has remained unresolved. This negative ion pathway is estimated to dominate over ice deposition on pre-existing dust grains in protoplanetary disk locations where there is sufficient UV to partially dissociate water molecules, and in addition, where negative ions such as OH- can form readily through electron attachment at low temperature.

papers.title: Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies
papers.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.

papers.title: A Statistical Analysis of Lopsidedness in Disk Galaxies
papers.abstract: We present a statistical analysis of Fourier lopsidedness in disk galaxies based on a deduplicated compilation of 606 unique objects: 442 have a measured m = 1 amplitude (A1), and 302 of these also have a measured m = 2 amplitude (A2), with no entry carrying A2 alone. The sample is a factor of approximately 3 larger than earlier homogeneous A1-A2 datasets. Our main results are: (i) Both A1 and A2 follow log-normal distributions (KS D = 0.046 and 0.048) which are strongly preferred over Rayleigh or exponential forms, pointing to a multiplicative amplification process rather than random-phase superposition. (ii) The m = 1 and m = 2 modes are correlated as A2 = 0.29 A1 + 0.11 (Spearman rho = 0.501, p less than 10^-19). (iii) A1 rises monotonically with morphological T-type from approximately 0.07 in E/S0 to approximately 0.37 in Sm/Im galaxies (Kendall tau = 0.234, p approximately 10^-12). (iv) A1 anti-correlates with gas rotation velocity (Spearman rho = -0.432) and, in a stellar-mass cross-matched subsample of 246 galaxies with independent stellar-mass estimates, with stellar mass (rho = -0.395). The weaker lopsidedness of massive, fast-rotating disks indicates that the observed m = 1 amplitude is regulated by internal dynamics rather than set by tidal perturbations alone. (v) The TNG50-1 simulation, analysed through the TNGGalaxyLab Fourier pipeline, reproduces the observed A1-stellar-mass anti-correlation with a nearly identical Spearman coefficient, although its median A1 is approximately 1.4 times lower, an offset consistent with the heterogeneous target selection of the observational compilation.

papers.title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
papers.abstract: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.

papers.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
papers.abstract: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$\alpha$ and Pa$\alpha$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$\alpha$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,\mu{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

papers.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
papers.abstract: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

papers.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
papers.abstract: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Pad\'e resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

papers.title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$$ contact interactions with an explicit $$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
papers.abstract: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $\Delta$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $\Delta$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $\Delta\Delta$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $\Lambda^2/\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}^2$, where $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}=\sqrt{2M_\Delta(M_\Delta-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$\Delta$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $\Delta$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$\Delta\Delta$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $\Delta\Delta$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.

papers.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
papers.abstract: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_\nu \gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

papers.title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
papers.abstract: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

papers.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

papers.title: Constraining electron heat flux from reduced measurements
papers.abstract: Coronal heating estimates depend partly on electron heat transport. Different electron velocity distributions can match the same observations yet carry different heat fluxes. We ask which measurements are enough to determine heat flux without finding how electrons are distributed across all speeds and directions. The solar wind carries electrons outward from the corona and allows their velocities to be measured directly. Using one Wind measurement, we keep density, mean flow, temperature and angular summaries for each energy channel. In the fixed-bin model, electron distributions that match these quantities have heat fluxes from 3.58 to 19.85 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$. Keeping the correlation between electron motion along and across the magnetic field fixes the heat flux at 11.73 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$, matching the original bin calculation. This recovers heat flux without reconstructing the full shape of the electron velocity distribution. When the measured counts vary, retaining the required correlations leaves the same heat-flux range as direct calculation from those counts. We propose testing coronal observations in the same way to find which features of electron motion they constrain well enough to determine heat transport. Those constraints could help establish the heating requirements used to assess coronal heating mechanisms.

papers.title: Tracing the Epoch of Reionization through extreme emission line galaxies around Cosmic Noon
papers.abstract: Star-forming galaxies at z>6 are thought to be the main drivers of cosmic reionization, but their faintness makes detailed study challenging even with JWST. Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems with intense nebular emission and are potential lower-redshift analogues of this population. We aim to assemble and characterize a statistically significant sample of EELGs in the CANDELS/EGS field around cosmic noon, and to assess their validity as analogues of the galaxies that drove reionization. We select EELG candidates from CANDELS photometry with a J-band color-excess criterion that identifies both H$\beta$+[OIII] and H$\alpha$ emitters. Physical properties are taken from CANDELS data products, and the selection is validated with MMT/MMIRS, Keck/MOSFIRE, HST/WFC3 and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, complemented by our own GTC/OSIRIS+ program. We identify 102 H$\beta$+[OIII] emitters at $z\sim1.7$ and 127 H$\alpha$ emitters at $z\sim1.0$. They are compact ($\sim$1.6 kpc), low-mass ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim8$) and strongly star-forming (sSFR $\sim10^{-8}$ yr$^{-1}$). Estimated purities of $84.3\pm1.5$\% (H$\beta$+[OIII]) and $76.8\pm2.0$\% (H$\alpha$) agree with spectroscopic confirmation rates (85\% and 63\%), with no evidence of significant AGN contamination. A joint Bayesian fit, corrected for completeness via a truncated likelihood, yields $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) = (6.71\pm0.16) + (3.31\pm0.46)\log(1+z)$, suggesting an evolution in the characteristic mass of the sample with cosmic time. We spectroscopically confirm a highly pure, AGN-free sample of cosmic-noon EELGs. While their mass scale evolves with redshift, their properties consistently match those of z>5 JWST extreme emitters, supporting them as intermediate-redshift analogues.

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
papers.abstract: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

papers.title: An Archival Search for Outer Solar System Objects in the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2: 65 Candidates, Including Four L4 Neptune Trojans
papers.abstract: I search the single-epoch detections of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (DECam, 2012-2019) for outer Solar System objects. Single-night detections are linked with a bound orbit model, vetted against artefacts, static sources and known objects, and confirmed by forced measurements on at least two new archival nights. The linker recovers 96% of known objects present on four nights in one sky tile, but end-to-end recall is about 7%, limited by cadence, tiling and catalogue incompleteness; no selection function is provided. Of 81 catalogue objects, four are designated; of the other 77, 53 are in evidence class A (multi-opposition, at least nine nights), 12 in class B and 12 in class C (not counted). On exposures never used in a fit, forced photometry detects 41 testable objects at 99% of predicted positions, as for known TNOs, against 6% at control positions; 22 pass a post hoc rule, 19 are inconclusive, none fails. Shifted controls were never confirmed by the archival image search (0 of 11,467) but were in 2.2% of trials by the catalogue precovery behind most scripted confirmations, so its nights alone are not sufficient. For the 65 class A and B candidates, 10-Myr integrations give four candidate L4 Neptune Trojans with 13-19 yr arcs, 21 resonant, 13 detached, nine scattering, two Centaurs and 16 classical objects; a detached class-B candidate has q=48.8 au. No object beyond 80 au was confirmed, which barely constrains Planet Nine. Positions are withheld until designation or 2027 June 30; their digests are published.

papers.title: Resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_7$ interference in $B X_s$ at NLO: Hard matching and radiative charm-loop jet function for $m_c 0$
papers.abstract: We study next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_s\gamma$ arising from the interference of the current-current operator $Q_1^q$ and the electromagnetic dipole operator $Q_{7\gamma}$. This contribution is among the main sources of theoretical uncertainty in Standard Model predictions for the decay rate. Using a factorisation theorem in soft-collinear effective theory for the kinematic endpoint region, $m_b-2E_\gamma=\mathcal{O}(\Lambda_{\rm QCD})$, we determine all previously unknown perturbative ingredients at NLO in the limit of a vanishing charm-quark mass, $m_c\to0$. Specifically, we compute the $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients, derive their renormalisation-group equations, and obtain accurate analytic approximations to their solutions by retaining the first two terms in a $1/N_c$ expansion. Our second main result is the two-loop correction to the radiative charm-loop jet function, including its full dependence on the collinear momentum fraction. Combining these results with the known $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ correction to the quark jet function and the one-loop renormalisation of the subleading shape function $g_{17}$, previously computed by some of us, we provide the first complete NLO description of this resolved contribution in the massless-charm limit. This leaves the $m_c$ dependence of the radiative charm-loop jet function as the remaining ingredient for a phenomenological analysis within renormalisation-group-improved perturbation theory.

papers.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
papers.abstract: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

papers.title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $$CDM
papers.abstract: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $\Lambda CDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $\Lambda CDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $\Lambda CDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $\gamma$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

papers.title: SHINE: Shear inference environment - Generative forward modelling for radio weak gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: Next-generation radio interferometers, such as SKA, will observe the radio sky with unprecedented sensitivity and resolution enabling weak gravitational lensing studies using radio data, which not only complement optical observations but also probe higher redshifts. However, traditional shear estimation methods, based on measuring the ellipticity of observed galaxies, are not directly applicable to radio interferometric data. Interferometric observations are acquired in the Fourier domain, where galaxy images are delocalised, making shape measurements non-trivial. Furthermore, deconvolution methods such as CLEAN can introduce systematic errors when converting observations to the image domain, biasing shear estimates. To address these challenges, we propose a cosmic shear inference method based on forward generative modelling, which avoids explicit shape measurements. Our forward model simulates galaxy images, applies the shear transformation and, by including the instrumental response of the radio interferometer, simulates the visibilities of observed galaxies, with the likelihood explicitly defined in Fourier space. Using Monte Carlo sampling algorithms, we estimate the posterior distribution of the cosmic shear conditioned on a set of galaxy observations that share a common shear. We obtain unbiased shear estimates with sub-percent accuracy when applied to parametric galaxy simulations. We compare our method to state-of-the-art shear estimators, demonstrating a reduction in uncertainty of up to 3 times and no apparent multiplicative bias. We then show that applying this parametric model to COSMOS galaxies with realistic morphologies introduces a bias in the shear estimate over 10{\sigma}. Finally, we demonstrate that, by incorporating a generative forward model based on an autoencoder architecture trained on real galaxy images, we can mitigate this bias to below the 2{\sigma} level.

papers.title: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
papers.abstract: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.

papers.title: Shot noise, aperture and resolution in Fourier measurements of disc lopsidedness: TNG50-1 and TNG100-1 analysed with TNGGalaxyLab
papers.abstract: We present TNGGalaxyLab, an open-source Python pipeline for particle-based Fourier decomposition of the stellar surface density of simulated disc galaxies. It measures m = 1-4 amplitude and phase profiles in the Rix and Zaritsky (1995) normalisation, handles IllustrisTNG snapshot conventions, and recovers injected amplitudes in synthetic discs to better than 2 per cent at N = 5 x 10^5. Fourier amplitudes are positive-definite, so Poisson noise biases them upwards by an amount that grows as the particle number falls. We measure a per-galaxy noise floor by randomising particle azimuths and define a noise-corrected amplitude A1,corr. Downsampling TNG50-1 discs to the TNG100-1 particle mass inflates the uncorrected A1 by 40-60 per cent, while A1,corr is recovered to within approximately 10 per cent. We then process all central galaxies with 3.16 x 10^9 < M*/Msun < 10^11 in TNG50-1 (915) and TNG100-1 (6717) with identical settings in the [1.5, 2.5] Rd aperture. Removing the bootstrap and shot-noise biases lowers the TNG100/TNG50 ratio of median A1 from 2.3 to 1.6. At fixed stellar mass, kinematically selected TNG100-1 discs remain 1.5-1.9 times more lopsided after correction; this excess persists whether the aperture is defined in Rd or in kpc, is not explained by kappa_rot or D/T, and is largest at 3.5-6 kpc. TNG50-1 is statistically consistent with the mass-matched S4G sample of Zaritsky et al. (2013); TNG100-1 is not. The low A1 reported for TNG100 by Lokas (2022) cannot be read as a resolution deficit, since with matched measurements TNG100-1 is more lopsided than TNG50-1. Code and catalogues are public.

papers.title: Towards a new model of the compact triple system $$ Tauri I. Improved periods and preliminary elements of the triple system
papers.abstract: We analysed our new radial velocity measurements and photometric observations (covering a time interval of 46838~days and 39100~days, respectively) as well as those from previous studies to derive accurate ephemerides for both orbits of the compact triple system $\lambda$ Tau. In the case of the inner eclipsing subsystem, we obtained a~linear ephemeris of T min.I=HJD 2440998.86069(35)+3.952952845(81)xE, improving the accuracy of the previous solutions by more than an order of magnitude. This allowed us to reproduce well all available light curve minima, including the first one recorded in 1844. Furthermore, the period of the outer subsystem, determined from radial velocity analysis, appears to be constant over the interval of available observations, with the corresponding linear ephemeris being T periast.=HJD 2456822.5(3.6)+33.02480(28)xE. Assuming near coplanarity of the inner and outer orbits, we estimated the preliminary physical properties of the whole system. We found that the secondary of the inner subsystem is filling or nearly filling its Roche lobe. We used the long-term stability of the eclipsing subsystem period to place a strong upper limit on the rate of the proposed episodic mass transfer to its primary component. Our results constitute a preparatory step for a follow-up study that will also include an analysis of a rich collection of optical spectro-interferometric observations and use a full-fledged numerical model to describe the evolution of the orbital architecture of the system. Particular attention will be focused on determining the inner orbit forced eccentricity and understanding the absence of the apsidal advance of the outer orbit in our present solution.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
papers.abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

papers.title: The $_c1(3872)$ Multiplet in the Diabatic Dynamical Diquark Model
papers.abstract: We apply a minimal form of the diabatic dynamical diquark model, which uses only dimeson thresholds augmented by constraints obtained from heavy-quark spin symmetry, to the hidden-charm tetraquark spectrum. We find that this model is insufficient to simultaneously reproduce the experimentally established states \(\chi_{c1}(3872)\), \(T_{c\bar c1}(3900)\), and \(T_{c\bar c1}(4020)\). We therefore extend the model to its complete form, by restoring the spin- and isospin-dependent diquark-antidiquark interactions from the original adiabatic dynamical diquark model into the full diabatic potential. Aligning the resulting framework to these three states allows the remaining members of the \(\Sigma_g^+(1S)\) multiplet to be predicted through coupled-channel scattering simulations. The resulting resonance or bound state locations lie within approximately \(10~\mathrm{MeV}\) of the corresponding pure adiabatic mass eigenvalue predictions in all cases, indicating that the adiabatic fine-structure pattern survives the inclusion of explicit dimeson channels. We also discuss possible experimental counterparts for the unconfirmed multiplet members.

papers.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
papers.abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $\omega_\alpha$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $\lambda_\alpha$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_\alpha$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

papers.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
papers.abstract: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $\gamma$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. Ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) have driven this revolution over the past two decades. In this plenary review, presented at the 9th Heidelberg International Symposium on High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy (Gamma 2026), I provide a synthesis of recent breakthrough physics discoveries achieved by current IACT arrays (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and VERITAS) alongside early scientific achievements from the Large-Sized Telescope prototype (LST-1) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key highlights include the definitive establishment of recurrent novae as transient cosmic-ray proton accelerators via RS Ophiuchi; spatially resolved multi-TeV emission from the relativistic jet termination shocks of microquasars; the discovery of a 20 TeV pulsed radiation component from the Vela pulsar, challenging established magnetospheric emission paradigms; precision measurements of the Galactic Center diffuse ridge spectrum favoring a high-energy cutoff; the detection of distant flat-spectrum radio quasars at $z \sim 1$ (OP 313 and PKS 0346-27), providing tight cosmological constraints on the Extragalactic Background Light; multi-wavelength afterglow detections of $\gamma$-ray bursts including GRB 221009A; and world-leading joint indirect dark matter limits from dwarf spheroidal galaxy and Galactic Center halo analyses. Together with algorithmic advances in deep learning reconstruction and the ongoing construction of CTAO, these milestones demonstrate the enduring vitality and future trajectory of ground-based $\gamma$-ray astrophysics.
authors: R. Lopez-Coto (Instituto de Astrofisica de Andalucia-CSIC)

papers.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
papers.abstract: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

papers.title: The PAU Survey: Dissecting strong-lensing systems with narrow-band photometric redshifts
papers.abstract: Wide-field imaging surveys such as Euclid will identify large samples of strong-lens candidates, whose scientific use requires redshifts for both deflectors and lensed sources. Source redshifts are challenging because faint arcs are blended with foreground light. We test lens-model-informed photometry on eight known strong lenses, using broad-band models to define component regions, point-reflection subtraction to reduce contamination, and PAU Survey narrow bands combined with five HSC or CFHT broad bands. BCNz estimates separate lens and source redshift distributions without imposing their expected ordering. All eight lens redshift peaks agree with spectroscopy within $|\delta_z|\leq0.014$, where $\delta_z=(z_b-z_{\rm spec})/(1+z_{\rm spec})$. Four source peaks, all at $z_{\rm s}^{\rm spec}\leq1.23$, agree within $|\delta_z|\leq0.025$. Symmetric subtraction reduces the median source $|\delta_z|$ from 0.336 to 0.071. At $|\delta_z|<0.05$, narrow- plus broad-band photometry yields eight lens and four source matches, versus three and two using EAZY with broad bands alone. These results demonstrate component redshift recovery in blended systems and support redshift-based lens-candidate assessment alongside morphology and colour. Larger narrow-band surveys, including J-PAS, could extend this approach, pending uncertainty calibration and blind candidate tests.

papers.title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
papers.abstract: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. LMC X-3 exhibits significant changes in both its spectral and timing properties between the two observing campaigns. Hardness-intensity and hardness-rms diagrams reveal a clear separation between the 2024 and 2025 observations and even within the 2024 observations. Overall, it indicates a transition from a relatively harder and more variable state to a brighter, softer, and less variable state. Power spectral analysis shows enhanced broadband variability during the 2024 observations, while the 2025 observations are characterized by weaker variability. Spectral modeling of the combined XSPECT observations indicates an increase in the thermal disk temperature from 0.8 to 1.17 keV, accompanied by a ~5 times increase in X-ray flux between the two epochs. The observed reduction in fractional rms variability with increasing source brightness and decreasing spectral hardness is consistent with more contribution from a stable thermal accretion disk. Taken together, the spectral and timing diagnostics provide a self-consistent picture of accretion-state evolution in LMC X-3, demonstrating the capability of XSPECT to probe long-term variability and accretion processes in bright black hole X-ray binaries.

papers.title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
papers.abstract:
Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. We analyze timing, flux, pulse-profile evolution, and spectra using EP, NICER, and IXPE X-ray observations. Results. We report a 2025 anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586, the largest in this source, with $\Delta
u\approx-1.174(7)	imes10^{-7}$ Hz and $\Delta
u/
u\approx-8.19(4)	imes10^{-7}$. Unlike its 2019 anti-glitch, this event was radiatively loud: the persistent X-ray flux roughly doubled (~106% increase), followed by a recovery exceeding 320 days. The pulse profile changed modestly but significantly: the valley between the main and secondary peaks became shallower and then recovered with the flux. Spectral properties also changed, and Fermi-GBM detected a short soft gamma-ray burst near the event. These features resemble the radiatively loud 2012 anti-glitch. Conclusions. 1E 2259+586 is unique among magnetars: its anti-glitch rate is comparable to normal spin-up glitch rates, and its anti-glitches can be radiatively loud or relatively quiescent. The fractional anti-glitch amplitudes appear to increase monotonically; further verification is needed. Regular monitoring of 1E 2259+586 is essential for understanding anti-glitch mechanisms.

papers.title: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
papers.abstract: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.

papers.title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
papers.abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. We analyse JCMT/POL-2 maps of nine NGC 1333 regions and ALMA Band 7 maps of two IRAS 4A regions. We estimate plane-of-sky field strengths and derive fluctuation spectra from polarisation-angle structure functions. Where these spectra are sufficiently constrained, we apply quasi-linear gyro-resonant theory to calculate CR pitch-angle scattering rates and $D(E)$. The measured fluctuations constrain CR scattering over proton energy intervals of approximately 0.24-5.3 PeV in NGC 1333 and 10-57 TeV in IRAS 4A. Within these intervals, $D(E)$ spans approximately $3\times10^{28}$-$10^{31}\,{\rm cm^2\,s^{-1}}$. Scattering varies substantially between regions and is stronger where the magnetic-field angular dispersion is greater. Extrapolation to common energies suggests scattering in IRAS 4A is one to two orders of magnitude stronger than its surroundings. Within the directly probed intervals, the scattering mean free paths exceed the individual region sizes. The inferred diffusion coefficients therefore characterise local scattering conditions. A cloud-scale diffusive regime requires CRs to sample multiple regions with different scattering rates. Dust polarisation observations therefore provide constraints on CR scattering in clouds, connecting scattering to cloud-scale transport at energies accessible to $\gamma$-ray observatories.

papers.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
papers.abstract: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

papers.title: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
papers.abstract: I present a comprehensive analysis of all publicly available NuSTAR observations of the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (2012--2024). The hard X-ray continuum is well described by thermal Comptonization in a hot corona, with electron temperatures $kT_{\rm e} \approx 40-125$ keV and optical depths $\tau \approx 0.4-1.2$ (slab geometry). A clear anti-correlation between $kT_{\rm e}$ and $\tau$ is observed, consistent with a thermostat behavior with constant Compton parameter $\gamma \approx 3.12$ calculated according to Sunyaev and Titarchuk (1980). Variability on timescales of hours constrains the size of the emitting region to $R \approx 250-1200 r_{\rm g}$, corresponding to moderate compactness values $\ell \lesssim 4$. The source occupies the same region of the compactness--temperature plane as other local Seyferts, with no evidence for pair runaway. I then explore two astroparticle implications. The IceCube neutrino excess reported toward NGC 4151 corresponds to $L_\nu/L_X \approx 0.3\%$, an energetically negligible contribution that does not alter the observed coronal energy balance. An additional injection of pairs from the hypothetical X17 boson cannot produce significant changes, unless the injection rate exceeds the photoproduction one, but no anomalies were found in the present data set. The NuSTAR data thus provide no evidence for either a significant neutrino cooling channel or an X17-related pair injection in the corona of NGC 4151.

papers.title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

papers.title: Two-component $$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
papers.abstract: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak. Our results lend further support to a physical picture in which high-energy cosmic rays are predominantly supplied by local sources, whereas low-energy cosmic rays arise mainly from the collective contribution of sources in other regions of the Galaxy. We also calculate the neutrino spectra of these sources, providing theoretical predictions for future tests of the model through observations of point-source and diffuse neutrino emission.

papers.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
papers.abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.

papers.title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
papers.abstract: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $\mu \propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

papers.title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
papers.abstract: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

papers.title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

papers.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources
papers.abstract: The elemental composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) must be evaluated at a given rigidity rather than energy to compare with candidate elemental abundances, such as those of low-energy cosmic rays seeding the acceleration of UHECRs. We determine the UHECR composition from fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data and evaluate the resulting abundances at fixed rigidity. We identify two classes of solutions consistent with measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV: one in which the hydrogen flux at Earth is dominated by secondary nucleons produced by photodisintegration of heavier nuclei in extragalactic photon fields, and a second in which this contribution is less pronounced. Only the latter, which yields a mixture of primary and secondary protons at Earth, allows a hydrogen abundance at the source comparable to that of low-energy cosmic rays. However, both classes of solutions require an overabundance of nuclei in the silicon-iron group. Other source models from the literature also fail to reproduce the full elemental composition. The metallicity of UHECRs thus differs markedly from that of all candidate seed populations considered, leaving the origin of the heavy-element excess unresolved.

papers.title: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform. Local holographic counterterms leave the metric unchanged, while mixed electric boundary conditions interpolate between the two ensembles and shift their stability limits.

papers.title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO
papers.abstract: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has detected photons with energies up to 3.7 PeV from the binary system Cygnus X-3 during a flaring episode. The combination of such extreme photon energies and the large source distance provides a sensitive probe of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV). In superluminal LIV scenarios, high-energy photons can become unstable and rapidly decay, resulting in a sharp spectral cutoff. However, the observed hard intrinsic spectrum of Cygnus X-3 exhibits no evidence for such a feature. This absence enables us to place stringent constraints on LIV, with the second-order LIV energy scale constrained to be above 10^{-2}M_{pl}, improving previous limits by nearly an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Non-singular cosmology from effective LQG-inspired black holes
papers.abstract: We propose a non-singular primordial cosmology derived from matching an effective Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an expanding Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker universe via Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The resulting modified Friedmann equation replaces the singularity with a quantum bounce in the Planckian regime. Mapping the surface energy-momentum tensor of the dynamic thin shell onto a homogeneous scalar field reveals a transient phantom-like behavior. For any equation of state of the shell satisfying $\omega > -1$, its effective energy density is diluted with cosmic expansion. Extending the framework to a two-scalar-field system provides a mechanism to bridge the energy gap between the Planckian bounce and the sub-Planckian scale. The pre-inflationary phase is brief, enabling the second scalar field to take over to drive the standard slow-roll inflation.

papers.title: Neutron stars nearly close the window for muon-induced baryon-number violation
papers.abstract: Baryon-number violation that needs a muon in the initial state can evade proton-decay searches and be observed in muon capture at Mu2e and COMET. Neutron stars contain muons, so the same interaction converts their protons into dark baryons, but the rate of this conversion in dense matter and its consequences have not been computed. In this paper we compute the conversion rate, the heat it deposits, and the evolution of a star under fast conversion. The coldest known neutron stars exclude conversion rates far below laboratory reach for every dark-fermion mass that capture in aluminium can produce, and faster conversion burns stars down or, unless conserved dark baryons repel each other strongly enough, collapses them. The repulsion they need follows a scaling law in the baryonic mass headroom of the nucleonic equation of state, which applies to any process that puts dark baryons in equilibrium with neutrons.

papers.title: A Virgo Environmental Survey Tracing Ionised Gas Emission (VESTIGE). XXIII. NGC 4569 past orbit reconstruction with ORFEO
papers.abstract: Extended ionised gas tails can preserve a dynamical record of a galaxy's recent interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM). Recovering that history from the observed tail requires solving an inverse dynamical problem tied to the physical conditions for gas removal. We present the first application of ORFEO to NGC 4569, using the sky positions and line-of-sight (LOS) velocities of the galaxy and 94 H$\alpha$-emitting regions to reconstruct its recent orbit and tail chronology. The model combines data with gas surface-density constraints, a spherical Virgo Cluster A gravitational potential derived with MG-MAMPOSSt, and an X-ray-based ICM density profile. For an assumed LOS distance, it infers its orbit and ram-pressure history. At the fiducial distance $d_0=16.5$ Mpc, ORFEO recovers a coherent phase-space sequence with a dynamical tail age $T_{\rm tail}=250^{+37}_{-19}$ Myr. The ram-pressure maximum occurred at $t_{P_{\rm ram},{\rm peak}}=-163^{+11}_{-15}$ Myr, close to the nearest approach to the Virgo Cluster A centre at $305^{+19}_{-25}$ kpc, placing NGC 4569 after peak ram pressure. Scanning the LOS distance does not select a unique solution but separates comparably fitting reconstructions into a low-distance post-peak branch and a high-distance pre-peak branch. Comparison with an independent stripping threshold at the observed disc truncation radius favours the low-distance solutions and supports a post-stripping interpretation. On this branch, ORFEO recovers the mostly west-to-east projected motion inferred from the H$\alpha$ morphology and is consistent with previous constraints on the interaction chronology. Requiring only $\sim10$--11 min of wall-clock time for NGC 4569, ORFEO provides a computationally inexpensive inverse framework for deriving orbital, tail, and ram-pressure histories that can guide tailored simulations and be extended to larger samples of stripped galaxies.

papers.title: Strong decays of $(3770)$, $(4040)$ and $(4160)$ in four relativistic wave-function representations
papers.abstract: Strong decays provide a direct test of the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions. We study the OZI-allowed hadronic decays of the vector charmonia $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$ and $\psi(4160)$ within the Salpeter equation, using four relativistic wave-function representations $\varphi_1$--$\varphi_4$ that differ in the $S$-, $P$- and $D$-wave components they retain independently, and the revised ${}^3P_0$ model. The quark-pair creation strength is fixed once, by reproducing the measured $\psi(3770)\to D\bar D$ width, and is not readjusted afterwards, so that the results for the two higher states are parameter-free predictions. The representation $\varphi_2$ predicts $94^{+34}_{-23}$~MeV for $\psi(4040)$ and $100^{+23}_{-20}$~MeV for $\psi(4160)$, in agreement with the measured $84.5\pm12.3$ and $69\pm10$~MeV, and it is the only one whose predicted width ratios are compatible with the data.
